Hi Emily — copying operational details below so legal and engineering can see the concrete controls. Marissa, please feel free to forward to Aurelia legal.

Summary of controls we can commit to for Aurelia Health (production workload):
1) No-model-learning enforcement
   - Production requests tagged with customer_id + opt_out flag. Requests with opt_out=1 will be routed to a non-learning inference path where logs are kept only for SLO/ops for 30 days (configurable).
   - We will not use production request data for model improvement, training, or research for the duration of the contract for any data tagged from Aurelia production systems.

2) Dataflow & subprocessor visibility
   - Attached: redwood-subprocessors-2027-06.csv (current subprocessor list) and dataflow-aurelia-2027-06.pdf (simplified mapping for your review).
   - Subprocessors that touch raw conversational payloads: FastKV (managed caching), GShardServe (inference runtime ops), and SecureLogs (S3-compatible encrypted storage).

3) Export & residency controls
   - We can enforce region routing (US-only) for all traffic originating from Aurelia production accounts. Backups and audit logs are stored in encrypted buckets in the us-east-1 region.
   - We can provide a sanitized export of logs and a signed attestation for the opt-out period on request quarterly.

4) Evidence & verification
   - Evidence package we can provide within 5 business days after contract effective date:
     * Signed operational runbook describing opt-out routing
     * Dataflow diagram and subprocessors (attached)
     * Short screencast (private link) showing opt_out flag in the console test harness

Limitations / follow-ups we need from Aurelia:
- Please confirm whether your sandbox/test connectors should inherit the same opt-out flag or if you want sandbox data excluded from the commitment.
- Any export/legal template language your counsel prefers for the DPA exhibit (we can propose a simple exhibit for "No Model Learning - Opt Out").

Attachments: redwood-subprocessors-2027-06.csv, dataflow-aurelia-2027-06.pdf

Thanks,
Stephanie

Thanks, Stephanie and Marissa. Helpful details. A few clarifying Qs from our side after we reviewed the checklist and the subprocessor list:

1) Can you confirm that the opt_out flag is customer-scoped (per-account) and not just per-request? We need a contractual guarantee that no future pipeline changes will cause our data to be ingested into training buckets unless explicitly agreed.
2) Which subprocessor(s) have access to decrypted conversational payloads for debugging? We ask because our security team will need to review their attestations and access controls.
3) For the quarterly attestation, will that include a signed hash of the representative logs and a statement of the retention policy applied?

Legal side: we attached a short redline of the DPA exhibit (high level) — primary ask is a one-sentence commitment plus remedies and an audit right for a third-party assessor (scoped and notice-limited). We'll send the redline to Marissa's team later today.

On scope: for now Aurelia requests the commitment to apply to production and pre-production (staging) environments. Sandbox/test projects that are explicitly used for experiments and are not connected to patient data can be excluded.

Appreciate the fast turnaround.

—Emily
Emily Richards
Head of Product — Integrations, Aurelia Health
